The Company has established five Committees: Audit Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Stakeholders Relationship Committee, Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, and Risk Management Committee.
The Board comprises 6 Directors as on March 31, 2026, out of which 3 are Independent Directors.
During FY 2025-26, 4 Board meetings were held with 100% attendance by all Directors.

The Company has adopted various codes and policies including Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, Vigil Mechanism and Whistle-Blower Policy, Policy on Materiality of Related Party Transactions, Corporate Social Responsibility Policy, Remuneration Policy, Risk Management Policy, Dividend Distribution Policy, and Data Privacy Policy.
The Company undergoes half-yearly secretarial compliance review by an independent company secretary in whole-time practice.
All related party transactions are reviewed and certified by an independent firm of Chartered Accountants.
The Company has appointed an independent firm of Chartered Accountants to conduct concurrent audit of share registry and other incidental functions carried out by the Share Transfer Agent.
Shares of the Company can be transferred/traded only in dematerialised mode as mandated by SEBI.
Members holding shares in physical mode are advised to avail the facility of dematerialisation.

The Company has implemented a legal compliance programme in conformity with best international standards covering Operating Management System, People Management System, and Financial Management System.
Periodical internal audits are conducted of all functions and activities. The Audit Committee regularly reviews the adequacy of internal control systems.
The Company has a budgetary control system to monitor expenditure against approved budgets on an ongoing basis.
The Company Secretary plays a key role in ensuring Board procedures are followed and assists the Chairman in management of Board's administrative activities.
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee works along with the Human Resource team for structured leadership succession planning.

risks: The nature of business of the Company does not involve Commodity Price risk or Foreign Exchange risk and accordingly does not require hedging activities.
Operational Risk: Pipeline operations may be disrupted due to natural calamities, equipment failures, or unforeseen events. A key risk is third-party damage to pipelines in high consequence areas.

Safety, Health and Environment Risks: Pipeline transportation of petroleum products and natural gas involves inherent hazards, including risks of accidents, leakages or external threats, which may impact life, property and the environment.

Environmental assessments and sustainability compliance have become substantive cost items, while the regulatory and reputational considerations in this area represent material risk factors for the sector.
Availability of skilled labour and volatility in input costs add further complexity to the overall business environment.
Liquidity risk: risk that suitable sources of funding for the company's business activities may not be available
Credit risk: risk that a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument will fail to perform or pay amounts due causing financial loss

Market risk: risk that the fair value of future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices (interest rate risk, currency risk, equity price risk, commodity risk)
Investment risk: return on plan asset below discount rate will create a plan deficit
Interest rate risk: fall in discount rate linked to G.Sec. Rate will increase present value of liability requiring higher provision
Salary risk: increase in salary of members more than assumed level will increase plan's liability
